text:
maya: Heads-up — seeing ~0.6% inter-region mTLS handshake failures since the RBAC tighten at 09:12 UTC. Logs point at KMS decrypt denies for the ephemeral keystore in ap-southeast-1. :rotating_light:

alex: On it. Can you paste the exact error snippet and the audit query you ran?

maya: Error excerpt:
```
2025-11-03T09:15:02Z ERROR handshake failed peer=svc-web-xyz region=eu-west-1: mTLS error: keystore unwrap failed: KMS.DecryptDenied: iam:Decrypt Deny principal=arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/keystore-reader/keystore-pod
  context: region_target=ap-southeast-1 resource=ephemeral-keystore-42
```

Also seeing this in the app-level logs when the client falls back to regional keystore: `ERR: tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: internal error`.

samir: Is this strictly cross-region traffic? East-west within the same region holding up?

maya: Mostly cross-region (ap-southeast -> eu-west calls failing). Same-region calls (ap-southeast -> ap-southeast) look fine. Pattern: requests routed to remote keystore endpoint that needs KMS unwrap in destination region.

jen: I deployed the RBAC change at 09:12 — we tightened the keystore-reader role to narrow ARNs. I think I may have omitted the ap-southeast alias in the resource list (typo). :facepalm:

kevin: If that matches the timeline it's likely the cause. Two questions: 1) do we have CloudTrail entries showing Deny for kms:Decrypt? 2) can we hotfix by re-adding the regional ARN?

maya: CloudTrail query I ran (truncated):
```sql
SELECT eventTime, userIdentity.principalId, eventName, awsRegion, errorMessage
FROM cloudtrail_logs
WHERE eventName = 'Decrypt' AND errorCode LIKE '%AccessDenied%'
  AND eventTime > '2025-11-03T09:10:00Z'
ORDER BY eventTime DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
Results: three Deny events 09:12:47, 09:13:11, 09:14:02 for principal `keystore-reader` targeting key arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01.

cert-rotator-bot: Rotator alert: 12 ephemeral cert rotations failed in eu-west-1 between 09:13-09:18 due to keystore unwrap error. Ticket created: #CR-4791.

alex: Short-term mitigation plan: revert the RBAC change for the keystore-reader role in ap-southeast-1 (re-add kms:Decrypt on the exact key ARN) and promote a canary for 10 minutes. If canary passes, roll forward a corrected PR. :thumbsup:

samir: Also worth checking whether the TLS fallback path is exposing us to different keystore selection. Handshake logs show occasional ClientHello SNI mismatch which could route to a different keystore instance.

maya: example openssl trace from a failing connection:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect services.example.com:443 -servername svc-web
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
SSL handshake has read 2123 bytes and written 319 bytes
New, TLSv1.3, Cipher is TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
*** TLSv1.3 Handshake Failure: Received fatal alert: internal_error
---
```
No obvious cert presented — probably the keystore unwrap aborted server side which triggers internal error.

jen: I'll open an emergency PR to re-add the ap-southeast ARN and tag oncall. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/PR/5123 (WIP). Triggering rollback now.

kevin: Post-mitigation items: 1) add aggregated metric/alert for KMS Decrypt Deny by principal (alerts when >5 denies/min), 2) add pre-deploy RBAC validator to CI for region-scoped ARNs, 3) expand rotator error telemetry to include KMS error codes.

alex: I'll draft the runbook entry for 'keystore KMS deny' and add the canary checklist. We should also add a short-term audit dashboard widget showing Deny count by region so SRE can catch regressions quickly.

jen: After rollback confirmed I'll run a control query for cert-rotator failures and mark the CR ticket as triaged. Follow-ups: validate service-account tokens used by rotator (sts assume role TTL), update deploy checklist to require region ARN test, and create a postmortem if >100 failures.

maya: Rolling state: after rollback (09:22) we saw handshake failures drop to 0.05% in the next 10m window. Will continue to monitor for 2h.

samir: Nice catch. For long-term, we should consider adding a local unwrap fallback (if secure) so cross-region kex doesn't brick traffic when a role scope misconfig happens. Also cipher/profile telemetry to catch protocol-level fallthroughs.

alex: Agreed. Action items assigned: jen (rollback + ticket), alex (runbook + dashboard), kevin (alert + telemetry), samir (fallback feasibility), maya (monitoring + final logs).

jen: tagging @oncall to confirm no outstanding issues. :white_check_mark:
